definition: India considered as a political and geographical community; not a synonym for the party in office.
A defined constitutional term for Part III that includes specified governmental institutions and authorities. It is wider than one constituent state.
Often the executive in office: ministers and the administration carrying out public decisions. Identify the institution when the word is being used more broadly.
A political organisation that may contest elections, govern, support a coalition or sit in opposition. It is not the same thing as the country.
The constitutional institution consisting of the President, Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha.
The House of the People, with representatives elected from territorial constituencies.
The Council of States. Its elected state representatives are chosen by elected MLAs using the constitutional indirect-election method.
Member of Parliament. Specify the House and the role when assessing a particular action.
Member of a Legislative Assembly. An Assembly and its state government are not interchangeable institutions.
Member of a Legislative Council, in a state where that institution operates. Councils and Assemblies have different composition and powers.
The executive group of ministers headed by the Prime Minister at Union level. It is collectively responsible to Lok Sabha.
The constitutional responsibility of the Council of Ministers to the relevant directly elected House: Lok Sabha at Union level and the Legislative Assembly at state level.
The political side outside the governing side that can scrutinise it and offer alternatives. This broad term is different from a formally recognised leadership office.
An electoral unit that returns a representative under the applicable system. Ordinary Lok Sabha constituency elections return one winner.
A constituency voting system in which the candidate with the most votes wins; an absolute majority is not required.
The list on which an elector must be included for the relevant election. Possession of an identity card is not a substitute for inclusion.
Electors Photo Identity Card. Identification and inclusion on an electoral roll are separate requirements to check.
A sworn statement. An election affidavit is a dated disclosure by a candidate, not a judicial finding that every allegation it records is proved.
A legislative proposal before enactment. A vote in one House does not automatically mean every required stage has been completed.
An enacted law. For practical application, check its commencement provisions and any later changes as well as assent.
A constitutionally defined category with a special parliamentary procedure. A proposal is not a Money Bill merely because it has a financial cost.
A rural local-government institution within the applicable constitutional and state-law arrangements. Do not assume identical powers everywhere.
An urban local-government institution whose actual powers must be established under the applicable law, not assumed from its location alone.
A budget-stage estimate for the specified financial year, not expenditure already completed.
An updated estimate for the specified year. It is still distinct from final reported actual expenditure.
Expenditure reported for a completed period under the source’s accounting scope. It does not by itself establish a service outcome.
In the budget presentation, the gap between total expenditure and receipts other than borrowing, under the stated accounting definitions.
Comptroller and Auditor General of India, the constitutional audit institution. An audit observation is not a criminal conviction.
Right to Information: access to information held by public authorities, subject to the applicable law. It is different from requesting a service repair.
Central Public Information Officer, the designated information officer in the Central RTI process. A portal nodal officer and the CPIO are not necessarily the same role.
A complaint seeking attention to a problem, such as a public-service failure. Its appropriate route depends on the subject and authority.
A claim that something happened or someone did something. The word alone establishes neither truth nor falsity.
Common terminology for a police report following investigation in the relevant procedural setting. It is distinct from a court-framed charge.
Release from custody under the applicable conditions and bond arrangement. It is not a judgment of acquittal.
A procedural outcome distinct from acquittal; the cited sessions-trial provisions concern whether there is sufficient ground to proceed before framing a charge.
The quantity above the division line: what is being counted in a fraction or rate.
The quantity below the division line: the population or total against which the numerator is compared.
The arithmetic difference between two percentages. A rise from 20% to 25% is five percentage points.
The time the evidence describes. It is not necessarily the year the report was published.
People in the labour force as a share of the relevant population, using the survey’s definitions and reference period.
Employed people as a share of the relevant population, under the stated survey measure.
Unemployed people as a share of the labour force, not of the entire population.
The original record relevant to a claim, such as an order, dataset or recording. Being original does not make it complete or infallible.
Additional evidence supporting a claim. Copies of one original story are not independent confirmations.
A conclusion drawn from evidence rather than a fact directly stated or observed. Make the reasoning and uncertainty visible.
A relationship or incentive that may affect a judgment. Document the relationship; do not treat its existence as automatic proof that every statement is false.
